patch.value: GH-772: rejected extension command registration leaves silent partial activation and zero-exit command gaps

When one extension command registration is rejected, earlier siblings remain active while the rejected and later commands disappear; invoking a dropped command yields misleading parent help or arity output with exit zero, and extension manage reports unknown activation state.

Rejected command registration cannot leave an undisclosed partially active surface; manifest-declared unavailable commands return a stable nonzero diagnostic; extension manage and help expose exact runtime activation status; real packed-extension tests cover rejection before, within, and after sibling command registrations.
pm 2026.7.27 with a command extension that collides with a host-owned global flag
Install pm-csv@2026.7.23 in a fresh workspace, inspect install diagnostics and extension manage, then invoke csv validate help and csv validate.
Extension activation is atomic or every unavailable declared command fails nonzero with its activation cause, and manage reports the same runtime status as health.
Earlier commands survive, the rejected and later siblings vanish, dropped command paths exit zero with misleading output, and manage reports runtime_active null and activation_status unknown.
